story.title: Hurricane Lala Affects Hawaii with Heavy Rain and Winds, Causing Flooding and Power Outages
story.summary: Hurricane Lala has brought heavy rain and strong winds to Hawaii's Big Island, causing significant flooding and power outages. The storm, which did not make landfall, has left over 89,000 households without power. At least one fatality has been reported due to a car accident in the affected area. The hurricane is expected to weaken gradually as it moves away from the island.

event_overview.title: About Approache Hurricane Storm
event_overview.subject: Approache Hurricane Storm
event_overview.summary: Hurricane Lala was a Central Pacific tropical cyclone that developed in mid-August 2026 and threatened Hawaiʻi, particularly the Island of Hawaiʻi. The storm strengthened from a tropical storm into a Category 1 hurricane while producing hazardous wind, rain and surf conditions near the state.

facts.label: Dates
facts.value: Lala formed as a tropical storm on August 13, 2026, and strengthened into a hurricane on August 15; the event was still unfolding as of August 16, 2026.

facts.label: Location
facts.value: The storm approached and passed near Hawaiʻi, with the Island of Hawaiʻi (the Big Island) facing the principal immediate threat; reporting on August 15 said its center skirted the island rather than making landfall.

facts.label: Intensity
facts.value: Lala reached Category 1 hurricane strength, with maximum sustained winds reported at 75 mph (120 km/h) on August 15.

facts.label: Forecast authority
facts.value: Tropical-cyclone outlooks and advisories for the Central Pacific, including the area around Hawaiʻi, are issued by the National Weather Service’s Central Pacific Hurricane Center in Honolulu in coordination with the National Hurricane Center.

facts.label: Naming and season
facts.value: Lala was listed as the first name in the 2026 Central Pacific tropical-cyclone naming sequence; the Central Pacific hurricane season runs from June 1 through November 30.

event_overview.scope_note: This timeline covers Lala’s approach to and effects on Hawaiʻi during August 15–16, 2026, not every advisory, local damage report, response action, or later stage of the storm.

explore_lenses.label: Why did Lala cause major damage without landfall?
explore_lenses.title: Outer storm bands can be the main hazard
explore_lenses.summary: Lala’s eye passed south of the Big Island, but its wind field and rain bands still reached the island. Forecasters and local officials stressed that a direct strike was not necessary for flooding, damaging winds and surf.

claims.text: National Weather Service meteorologist Joseph Clark said landfall was no longer expected after Lala’s eye passed the island’s southern tip, but the storm had already brought flooding and strong winds.
Forecast: The National Hurricane Center said hurricane-force winds could continue overnight, while rain into Sunday could produce flooding and mudslides and waves could continue to affect the coast.
Before the storm arrived, National Weather Service meteorologist Vanessa Almanza warned that many impacts occur outside a hurricane’s core, including heavy rain, wind and coastal hazards.

explore_lenses.label: Which communities face the greatest risks?
explore_lenses.title: Remote areas and utility-dependent households are exposed
explore_lenses.summary: The storm’s risks are especially acute in rural and mountainous parts of the Big Island, where access can be constrained by flooded or blocked roads and some residents live in off-grid or improvised housing. Long outages also pose added risks for people relying on powered medical equipment.

claims.text: State Rep. Jeanné Kapela identified the island’s remote southern communities, including people living off grid in unpermitted structures, as a particular concern as conditions worsened.
A local fire captain told AP that flash flooding and fallen albizia trees were key concerns because the large, relatively weak trees can make roads impassable.
Hawaiian Electric advises people dependent on electrically powered life-support equipment without backup power to arrange to go to a location with power after a storm or evacuation.
As of August 15, Gov. Josh Green said one person had died in a South Point-area car crash, 19 roofs had been lost and 190 flights had been postponed.

explore_lenses.label: What happens next as Lala moves away?
explore_lenses.title: Hazards may outlast the closest pass
explore_lenses.summary: The immediate question is whether rain, surf and wind hazards diminish quickly enough for safe road access and power restoration. Warnings remained beyond the Big Island as Lala moved west.

claims.text: Forecast: The National Hurricane Center expected Lala to gradually weaken after passing the Big Island, but warned that rainfall, mudslide risk, strong winds at higher elevations and dangerous surf could continue into Sunday.
Tropical-storm warnings remained in effect for Maui, Molokai, Lanai, Kahoolawe, Oahu, Kauai and Niihau as the storm moved west.

Forecast: Forecasters projected 8 to 12 inches of total rain across Maui and lower elevations of the Big Island, 4 to 6 inches across the island chain, and up to 25 inches in higher Big Island terrain.
Hawaiian Electric says its outage-map customer counts and restoration estimates are approximate and can be delayed when multiple outages occur.

story_report.summary: Hurricane Lala brought heavy rain and strong winds to Hawaii’s Big Island, causing significant flooding even though its eye passed south of the island and landfall was no longer expected. More than 89,000 households lost power, and Gov. Josh Green reported one death in a South Point-area car crash, along with 19 roofs lost and 190 postponed flights. The storm was forecast to weaken gradually after moving past the island, but hazardous weather was expected to persist.

sections.heading: Remote Communities Face Added Risks
sections.body: State Rep. Jeanné Kapela said remote southern communities were a particular concern, including people living off grid in unpermitted structures. A local fire captain cited flash flooding and fallen albizia trees as key hazards because the large, relatively weak trees can block roads. Hawaiian Electric advises people who rely on electrically powered life-support equipment and lack backup power to arrange to go to a location with power after a storm or evacuation.

sections.heading: Warnings Continue Across Hawaiian Islands
sections.body: Tropical-storm warnings remained in effect for Maui, Molokai, Lanai, Kahoolawe, Oahu, Kauai and Niihau as Lala moved west. The National Hurricane Center said hurricane-force winds could continue overnight and warned that rain, flooding, mudslides and coastal waves could continue into Sunday. Forecasters projected 8 to 12 inches of total rain across Maui and lower Big Island elevations, 4 to 6 inches across the island chain, and as much as 25 inches in higher Big Island terrain.

unresolved.text: Authorities had not fully itemized the extent to which wind, rainfall or local infrastructure failures caused particular flooding, outages and roof losses.

The reporting did not establish whether storm conditions directly caused the fatal South Point-area crash, and it did not identify how many outage-affected customers needed medical or shelter assistance.

As of August 16, final rainfall totals, the number and duration of outages, road-reopening timelines and the full damage assessment remained unresolved; Hawaiian Electric says outage-map customer counts and restoration estimates are approximate and may be delayed during multiple outages.

related_stories.title: Hurricane Lala Approaches Hawaii, State of Emergency Declared
related_stories.summary: Hurricane Lala has strengthened and is on a forecast track toward Hawaii's Big Island, with potential landfall expected this weekend. If it makes landfall, it would mark the first direct hit from a hurricane on the island in 155 years, since 1871. Authorities have declared a state of emergency in preparation for heavy rain and strong winds associated with the storm.

related_stories.title: Fatal Polish Bus Crash in Hungary Leaves Twelve Dead and Many Injured
related_stories.summary: A Polish tourist bus overturned on the M3 motorway in Hungary, resulting in the deaths of twelve people and leaving at least ten others seriously injured. The incident occurred near the town of Mezőkeresztes in the early hours of Sunday morning. Local police indicated that the bus veered off the road into a ditch, and early reports suggest that the driver may have fallen asleep before the crash.

related_stories.title: Tributes and Calls for Reflection Following Jason Arday's Death
related_stories.summary: Jason Arday, a British sociologist and former professor at the University of Cambridge, was found dead following his resignation amid plagiarism allegations. His death has prompted tributes from friends and calls for reflection from British leaders, who described the situation as a tragedy and a moment for introspection regarding race and hiring practices in academia.

related_stories.summary: The death toll from the ferry capsizing on Lake Kariba in Zimbabwe has risen to 72, according to police reports. Authorities have recovered 25 bodies as the search for additional victims continues following the tragic incident earlier this week.
